Tap the glowing dots

This is Yazd, a city in Iran. The houses look very different from ours. Find 4 clues about how people live – and sleep – here.
🗣 Talk: On a 40°C night with no air-conditioning, where would you sleep – on the roof, in the courtyard, or on the floor inside? Why?

Hands up: Who has ever slept outside? Who has slept on the floor? (That's exactly how our story begins.)

Mountains to the north, desert to the south. Flat roofs everywhere.
🗣 Ask: How would you get from Shenzhen to Teheran? How long would it take? What would you pack for 40°C days and cool nights?

Vocabulary · Drag & drop

Words in action

Then personalise: "I'm saving up for…" / "I once smashed … to pieces." / "I glanced at … and saw…"

Grammar · Past perfect

Tap the action that happened first

1
2
Two past actions. The one that happened earlier takes had + past participle. Tap the verb you think came first.

Pattern to drill: "He didn't … until … had …" / "After … had …, … ."

Grammar · Sentence surgery

Cut "Because he was…" – start with -ed / -ing

➜
Rule: the person doing the -ing / feeling the -ed must be the subject of the main clause. ✗ Glancing at the wood, the mattress was picked up. (A mattress can't glance!)

Students say the shorter version aloud first, then reveal.

Press SPIN. Example:  For the first time in her life, my grandma used a smartphone to order dinner.
Bonus point: end your sentence with a time or place adverbial.

Wrap-up

So… was it really the end of the dream?

💬 Talk

  • He "sadly picked up the mattress" but "promptly went to sleep again". Is he sad or happy? Why?
  • Change ONE thing to change the ending: If he had tied the bed to the roof…
  • What's the funniest or saddest thing that has happened to something you saved up for?

📝 Homework

  • Retell the story in 60–80 words. Use not…until…had, After…had, and ONE sentence starting with -ed/-ing.
  • Sentence Builder Level 5 (Combine + Fix).
  • Three true sentences: For the first time in my life, …

Exit ticket: everyone leaves with one sentence beginning "Tired of…".
